newsitem.title: USA: San Antonio, Texas, elec. deal raised to $661 mln.
newsitem.headline: San Antonio, Texas, elec. deal raised to $661 mln.

text.p: San Antonio, Texas' electric and gas bond sale was increased to $661 million from $486 million after favorable market conditions made more of the city utility's outstanding bonds eligible for advance refunding, an official said Wednesday.

"We were very fortunate to have an improvement in the market from an issuer's side," Donald Thomas, secretary-treasurer of City Public Service, said, citing a downward interest-rate trend over the past week or so.

While the Tuesday offering's new money piece remained constant at $350 million, the advance refunding portion was increased to roughly $311 million from the $131 million contemplated on Monday, he said.
The preliminary official statement listed the deal's total as $486 million, a figure that grew to $599 million by the preliminary pricing.
Senior manger PaineWebber Inc later repriced the deal, trimming yields by five basis points in most maturities.
The biggest cut was in the 1998 maturity, where the yield was lowered by 10 basis points to 3.85 percent from 3.95 percent.
The offering's top yield remained unchanged at 5.75 percent in 2020. Investor interest in the deal was "broad-based," Thomas said.
Bonds being refunded came from issues in 1988, 1989, 1991 and 1992, he said.
The utility achieved an average present value savings of just over three percent, or slightly more than $9 million with the deal.
Thomas said the offering still needs approval from the City Public Service Board of Trustees and from the San Antonio City Council.
Separate meetings are set for Thursday, he said.
